title: Capturing Thought Dynamics: Modeling the Structure of Spontaneous Associations
summary: A model trained on roughly 126,000 Hebrew word-association pairs quantified the breadth and temporal structure of spontaneous associations. Across two participant samples, nonlinear patterns in these measures related to self-reported rumination and repetitive thinking, while simple linear relationships were not reliable. The result concerns questionnaire associations and does not establish a clinical diagnostic measure.
ai_technology: Random-forest Associator trained on human association norms and word-embedding features quantified associative strength.
organization: Bar-Ilan University; University of Haifa; Jönköping University

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: The Associator model was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation; derived measures were analyzed across two participant samples.
evidence.unknown: Self-report associations and task-specific measures; ecological validity and clinical use remain limited.
